lesson.title_tag: Professor View -- Stephanie Santin | Lesson 6 -- Second Conditional

listenings.text: People always ask me if I would go back. Honestly, I do not know. If someone offered me a research year abroad tomorrow, I think I would say yes, but the answer is not simple. My daughter is eleven. If she were three, I would take her and she would learn the language in a month. At eleven it is different. And if I left for a year, I would lose the position I have here, because nobody keeps a job open that long. So my honest answer is this: if the offer came with six months instead of twelve, I would go tomorrow. Twelve months, I would have to think very hard.

I get this question from Brazilian doctors every month, so let me be direct. If I were starting this process today, I would do three things differently. First, I would take the English exam before anything else, because it is the slowest part and everybody leaves it for the end. Second, I would write to the researcher directly instead of writing to the department, because departments do not answer and people do. Third, I would ask for three months, not a year. A short visit is much easier to approve, and if it goes well, the second one is almost automatic. That is what I would do. What you do is your decision.
